tierWindow.goal: Synthesise how you succeed at university as a self-regulating learner, evaluate the graduate capital you are building, and define success on your own terms as you become a graduate.
tierWindow.cognitiveDemand: Synthesis, evaluation and self-directed articulation: relate frameworks to your own development and justify judgements about it.
tierWindow.taskComplexity: Integrative and open, holding several ideas together at once, with your own degree and development as the case rather than a tidy single example.
tierWindow.autonomy: Low scaffolding; you direct the application to your own situation; feedback extends and challenges rather than simply confirms.

decidedValue.priorExperienceAnchor: The learner is well into their degree, often approaching graduation. They have met the excelling mindset and have put motivation and goal-setting into action; the task now is to own and articulate their development, naming the success and the graduate capital they can already evidence.

decidedValue.signpostBody: The course has three short lessons. First, the engine of succeeding: self-regulated learning and self-efficacy, the resources that keep you going. Second, graduate capital: the framework that reframes success and its five forms. Third, defining success and becoming a graduate: setting your own terms and articulating what you can evidence. Work through them in order; each builds on the one before.
decidedValue.signpostInstruction: Work through the three lessons in order.
decidedValue.overview:
This course is about succeeding at university as you reach the end of your degree. Succeeding is more than good marks. It is learning to direct your own study, building the capital a graduate carries into work and life, and being able to say, with evidence, what you have become. By the end you will be able to appraise how self-regulated learning and self-efficacy sustain your success, evaluate the graduate capital you are building across its five forms, and define success on your own terms.

At this stage the question is no longer how to start. It is how to own and articulate what you are already doing. Employers, interview panels and your own plans all ask you to make your development explicit. This course helps you name it.
decidedValue.courseOutcomesFraming: Three course outcomes framed up front: appraise the engine of succeeding, evaluate your graduate capital, define and articulate your own success.

practiceConnection.academic: Succeeding at university is the rehearsal for succeeding beyond it. The habits of a self-regulating learner, the capital you build, and the ability to articulate your development are exactly what graduate recruiters, professional bodies and research supervisors look for. The work you do here is the work of becoming a graduate, not a bolt-on to it.

decidedValue.summary: You have reached the end of the course. Succeeding at university is no longer just a grade. You can appraise the engine behind it, self-regulated learning sustained by self-efficacy. You can evaluate the graduate capital your degree is building across its five forms. And you can define success on your own terms and articulate, with evidence, what you have become. Look back at the confidence check: comparing where you started with where you are now shows how far this has moved.

practiceConnection.academic: From here, these are not study ideas but working habits. Every application you write, every interview you sit, every supervision or appraisal you attend, asks you to regulate your own work, show the capital you bring, and articulate your development with evidence. The course has rehearsed exactly that. Succeeding at university and succeeding beyond it draw on the same moves.
